scores.Rationale: The proposal addresses an important unmet need by combining smartphone sensor data with caregiver/passenger real-time observations and Michon’s model to extend clinic-based driving assessment into naturalistic settings. While elements (GPS/sensor driving studies, digital biomarkers) exist in the literature, the dyadic passenger-observer integration and explicit clinical translation for Long Island rehabilitation services represent a meaningful and potentially scalable innovation.

The high-level study design (correlating app-derived measures with standardized clinical tests) is appropriate and a realistic timeline is provided, and existing pilot work and clinical referral pathways are strengths. However, key methodological details are missing (target sample size, power/sample justification, specifics of sensor/data processing, statistical analysis plan, data security/privacy, and contingency plans), which limits assessment of rigor and feasibility.

The PI has strong, relevant expertise in mobile health and digital phenotyping and an established track record of funded and published work; the Co-PI is uniquely qualified as the only DRP with a healthcare background on Long Island. Commitment from neurology faculty is noted, providing useful interdisciplinary clinical support for recruitment and clinical relevance.

The project aligns well with likely foundation funders (AOTF, Mother Cabrini, ASAHP) and the team outlines concrete follow-up grant targets and timelines, making future funding plausible. Competitiveness for larger federal funding will depend on stronger pilot data, clearer methods, and demonstrated feasibility from this seed study.

The single-line budget request for a UFOV assessment tool is justified as important, but the budget lacks detail on other anticipated costs (participant incentives, software/platform maintenance, data storage, personnel time, IRB fees), and the budget table contains placeholder/NaN entries, limiting transparency and cost-effectiveness assessment.

The application is generally well organized with clear aims and a coherent justification for the work; background and impact are well articulated. Some sections are repetitive, a few timeline details and tables are messy, and methodological specifics are under-specified which reduces clarity for reviewers.
